description: We are a team of curious tech enthusiasts passionate about innovation, problem-solving, and space exploration. Our interests include AI/ML, Data Science, Python, Web Development, and emerging technologies. We believe in learning, sharing ideas, and building solutions together. We welcome creative and motivated participants with skills in coding, UI/UX design, data analysis, astronomy, research, and presentation. Let's collaborate, think beyond limits, and create something impactful!
summary:
ARES (Adaptive Reconnaissance & EVA Safety System) is an intelligent, multi-mission Mars exploration and route-planning platform designed to support future human explorers. It integrates scientific observations from NASA missions, including HiRISE, MOLA, CRISM, THEMIS, and Perseverance, into a unified interactive Martian map.

ARES combines geospatial analysis, terrain hazard assessment, scientific target identification, and uncertainty-aware multi-objective route optimization. Unlike conventional shortest-path navigation, it evaluates potential routes using terrain safety, scientific value, mission resource requirements, data confidence, and return feasibility. It also identifies gaps in scientific observations rather than assuming unexplored terrain is safe.

The platform addresses the challenge by transforming distributed planetary science data into actionable exploration intelligence. Its purpose is to help astronauts plan safer Marswalks while identifying scientifically valuable locations, maximizing mission efficiency, and supporting informed decisions during exploration.
details:
ARES (Adaptive Reconnaissance & EVA Safety System) is an AI-powered Martian exploration and mission-planning platform designed to support future human explorers. It integrates scientific observations from multiple NASA missions into a unified interactive 2D/3D Martian map, initially focusing on the scientifically rich Jezero Crater region.

The platform combines terrain intelligence, geological analysis, hazard assessment, scientific target identification and uncertainty-aware multi-objective route optimization. Instead of selecting routes based only on distance, ARES evaluates terrain safety, scientific potential, data confidence, estimated mission costs and return feasibility. Its Evidence-Aware Multi-Objective Route Intelligence (EMRI) engine aims to help explorers balance scientific discoveries with mission safety.

The project is designed to transform distributed planetary datasets into understandable, actionable exploration information. Its intended impact is to support safer surface exploration, improve scientific mission planning and help identify valuable geological targets.

The planned technology stack includes Google AI Studio for AI-assisted development, React and TypeScript for the interactive interface, Python and FastAPI for backend services, and geospatial tools such as Rasterio, GeoPandas, NumPy and NetworkX for scientific data processing and route optimization.

ARES introduces a creative, evidence-aware approach by explicitly representing missing observations, uncertainty and alternative routes rather than assuming that unexplored terrain is safe. Key considerations include scientific accuracy, NASA data reliability, terrain hazards, mission resource constraints, usability, transparency and reproducibility.
